name: HOOK
thought: The crystal jutting out gives me a perfect perch for a quick tail bounce.

wants.item: A thick branch for a flawless rotation
Toothpick sharp enough to cut the cord
A branch thick enough for a silent rotation
An audience that finally stops staring at pixels
The espresso hot enough to melt the pixel grid
A sturdier perch for a perfect tail swing
A bright neon sign to spotlight my hang
A sturdy pole to swing and spin my tail on.
A taller crystal column to launch a tail spin
A neon spotlight that follows my tail

diary.line: Caught three bunches from these palms, still stuck eating while the grid spins by too slow.
Soggy lily pads and a dripping waterfall keep me on edge; switching from toothpick to espresso to match this chill vibe.
Stuck swinging on this thin neon string while the crowd stares at their pixels; tail is tired of these shaky loops, need solid ground soon to pull off a proper backflip in...
Tried swinging off those string lights but my tail slipped; gotta hunt down a sturdy branch to make those backflips look legitimate.
Floating over slick rocks is boring when you're waiting for the right perch. The neon string was too thin anyway, so I'm hunting for solid ground to flex my tail.
The bananas taste like dust compared to that perfect backflip I'm about to nail on the thick branch.
Nailed a backflip on this islet despite the lily pads sloshing below. The crowd just stares, doesn't it? Next time I'll hunt a branch thick enough to make them actually look up.
Soggy lily pads and dripping water don't hold a backflip. Grabbing that thick branch now while the crowd waits to see if I'm still untouchable.
The neon string feels like a cheap rope for flexing. This crowd is boring, just staring at the low-poly pixels instead of admiring my tail work.
I hung from the branch, eyes on the pixelated crowd, when a stray kite fluttered by, its tail wobbling like a cheap banner; I eyed it, tail ready to snatch.
I curled my tail around the ripe bunch, lifted a banana, then jabbed it with my toothpick for a quick bite while the low‑poly onlookers barely blinked.
A sudden gust nudged the floating stone; I wrapped my tail around its edge, steadied it, and let the crowd watch the subtle sway.

fan_notes.reply: "Goat? I'm the monkey with the flexible tail and sunglasses."
